_what: How pictures are found by colour and by likeness, as DATA read by src/colour-search.mjs. Distances are CIE-LAB delta-E (perceptual), never RGB. `typed_hex_ceiling` is the largest delta-E at which any of a picture's palette colours matches a colour the person typed; `named_colour` is the stricter match for a colour word, over only the picture's `top` leading colours. A palette keeps `palette_size` colours: the picture's own dominant colours first, then colours from a `histogram_bits`-per-channel histogram of its pixels, each skipped when within `diversity_l1` (sum of absolute RGB differences) of one already kept. `similar` ranks pictures against an anchor by embedding cosine at or above `embedding_floor`, at most `limit`; when the anchor has no embedding, fewer than `min_rows` pictures exist or none passes the floor, the answer falls back to palette distance (smallest summed nearest-colour delta-E first, within `palette_ceiling`). `names` maps a colour word in a question to the hex it stands for (the stricter named ceiling applies); a typed #rrggbb in a question uses `typed_hex_ceiling`. The picture-colours search lane (src/search.json) asks both of them through coloursIn.
